title: Control Flow
summary: Making decisions with if, else if and else, the switch statement and switch expressions, loops with while, do-while, for and foreach, break and continue, nested loops, and input loops that keep asking until the input is valid.

cards.q: When does a do-while loop differ from a while loop?
cards.a:
A do-while always runs its body at least once, since it checks the condition after it

The condition of a do-while is tested after the body, so the body runs once even when the condition is false from the start.

cards.q: What does continue do inside a for loop?
cards.a:
Skips the rest of this round's body, runs i++, then goes on with the next round

`continue` ends only the current round. In a for loop the update part (`i++`) still runs before the condition is checked again.
